resources.string: Android development slice. S10 runs the app or game; A06 views and manually controls it over a paired, encrypted local connection. No audio, cloud, macros, or game-specific assistance.
No game is officially supported. COD compatibility, latency, thermals, and account safety are unverified. Secure or locked screens may not be captured or controlled.

1. Orient the Host before sharing. Open an invitation on an existing LAN interface.
2. Privately transfer it to the Client and connect.
3. Start screen sharing with Android consent.
4. Optionally allow single-finger control for one selected app.
Allow control and open selected app

Paste the Host invitation through a trusted, private channel. Verify the full Host fingerprint with its screen before connecting. Invitations expire after 2 minutes and are single-use. Reconnection always requires a new invitation and new capture consent.
Allow manual control for this session?

The paired Client may touch only %1$s while that app is the active, unobscured window. Only one finger is supported, with bounded holds. Android may reject injected input; immediate raw ACTION_CANCEL is not available. This does not establish game compatibility or account safety. Leaving the target or losing consent stops control. No permission is enabled automatically.

Compare this with the Host. This connection grants viewing only; the Host must separately start capture and allow control.

Optional manual touch control from a paired Client. Enable only if you consent. Every session also requires Allow Control on this phone for one selected user-installed app. The service checks active-window package and security metadata; it does not read, retain, or transmit text or the window tree. It cannot unlock the phone or approve system permissions. Single-finger input only; release is best-effort through public Android APIs. No macros or game assistance.
Manual, app-scoped control; separate approval every session.
Accessibility is optional and must be enabled manually in Android settings. On Android 13+, sideloaded apps may be subject to Android restricted-settings protection. No setting is changed for you.
